base: black-and-white editorial vintage documentary photograph, desaturated, high contrast, grainy film texture. WIDE HORIZONTAL LANDSCAPE orientation, 3:2 aspect ratio, much wider than tall. FRAMING IS CRITICAL: the camera is CLOSE and the subject is VERY LARGE, filling the entire BOTTOM THREE QUARTERS of the frame from the left edge to the right edge, extending past the bottom edge. Only a NARROW BAND across the very TOP of the frame, about one fifth of the height, is empty pale bright almost-white wall or light, completely free of objects. EVERYTHING IS IN SHARP CRISP FOCUS, deep depth of field, no blur, no bokeh, no soft focus. This is ONE single real photographic exposure, never a composite: every element shares the same light and grain. THE TOP OF THE FRAME IS BRIGHT OVEREXPOSED LIGHT, and the transition from the scene into that light is GRADUAL and soft, as if the light swallows the upper part of the scene: NO horizontal edge anywhere, no shelf edge, no ceiling line, no sign, no roofline crossing the top. Surfaces and objects fade softly upward into the light. THE TOP BAND IS A HARD REQUIREMENT: that top fifth must be ONE single continuous evenly-lit pale surface spanning the FULL width, bright and uniform, with NOTHING crossing it at all: no shelf, no beam, no lamp, no head, no edge of any object. It must read as smooth blank paper. NO fog, NO mist, NO haze and NO smoke anywhere inside the scene itself; only that narrow band at the very top is pale. Natural unposed body language. Brazil; every sign, card, notebook, photograph, uniform or object in the scene is PLAIN and UNBRANDED: no printed brand names, no logos, no legible writing of any kind; any papers, notebooks, punch cards or photographs show only vague illegible marks, never readable letters or numbers. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no emojis, no gradients, no added color, no stock photo look.
cinema: CINEMATIC DIRECTION: camera at chest height, one strong directional light source raking across the scene, deep shadows, dramatic contrast. People LARGE and CLOSE, chest up, heads at about one fifth from the top of the frame. Every person is FULLY inside the frame: heads complete with clear empty space above them, nobody cropped at the neck, shoulders or waist, nobody touching the left or right edges.
fit: COMPOSITION FOR THE SLIDE (HARD REQUIREMENT): the subject occupies ONLY the LOWER 55 percent of the frame; the ENTIRE UPPER 45 percent of the frame is a plain, flat, evenly lit surface in a very pale OFF-WHITE tone (like unbleached linen paper, hex F3F3F3), with a faint fine texture and absolutely nothing on it: no shelves, no objects, no doorway, no window, no sign, no ceiling line, no heads. That pale surface is part of the photograph and simply continues upward, staying very pale and uniform to the top edge.

images.scene: Brazil, 1970s, a small company office counter: a wooden cash drawer pulled open, full of banknotes, and a STRANGER'S HAND in a dark suit sleeve with a stiff white cuff reaching in from the right and lifting a thick bundle of the notes out, while on the left the owner's hand, in a rolled-up shirt sleeve, rests flat on the counter, too late. Only the two hands and forearms, large and close. No faces.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life on a wooden desk: a blank tax payment form (only vague illegible marks) clipped with a metal binder clip to a desk calendar whose pages are flipped several weeks ahead, an old fountain pen lying beside it: the tax that will only be paid later. NO PEOPLE, no readable text.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life on a wooden office desk: a thick bundle of banknotes held by a rubber band lying on top of a spread of payment slips, invoices and a payroll envelope, next to a rubber stamp and an ink pad. The money sits on top of the bills it is about to pay. NO PEOPLE, no readable text.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life on a shop counter: a long paper receipt tape coming out of an old mechanical cash register, and a big pair of steel scissors in the middle of cutting the tape in two, the two halves curling apart. NO PEOPLE, no readable text.

Brazil, 1970s, a wide low view of an enormous floor covered with endless rows of identical stacked cardboard archive boxes, kept LOW, stacks no taller than the lower half of the frame, receding into the distance: the size of a huge number. NO PEOPLE, no readable text.

Brazil, 1970s, a bank manager's desk seen close: across the desk the BANKER's hands in a dark suit push a long loan contract and a fountain pen toward the business OWNER, whose hand hesitates above the signature line. Hands, forearms, contract and pen large and close; at most the torsos, no faces above the shoulders.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life on an owner's desk: a folded newspaper (only illegible grey columns, no readable headline) with a pair of heavy reading glasses resting on it and a cup of black coffee gone cold beside it. NO PEOPLE, no readable text.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE: an old metal flashlight lying on a wooden floor, its beam lighting up a large dark crack and broken hole between the floorboards that had been hidden under a pulled-back rug. NO PEOPLE, no readable text.

Brazil, 1970s, an empty wooden harbour pier seen low and close: a round life buoy hangs from a weathered wooden post, rope coiled at its base, calm water behind kept low in the frame. NO PEOPLE, no readable text.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life: an old mechanical adding machine on the edge of a desk with a very long paper tape of calculations spilling off the desk and curling onto the floor (only illegible marks). NO PEOPLE, no readable text.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life on a desk: a spiral desk calendar with many pages already flipped over the top ring, a pencil lying across it, pages show only vague illegible marks. NO PEOPLE, no readable text.

Brazil, 1970s, CLOSE still life on a wooden desk: a thick open accounting ledger with neat handwritten columns (illegible), a fountain pen across it and an old cast-iron coin bank beside it: a business owner who knows his numbers. NO PEOPLE, no readable text.
